title: The grounding column mixes three unlike measures and one of them is not a vocabulary lookup [corrected 2026-11-05 — the circularity claim in this block was wrong; see §6a]
recommended_action: [superseded 2026-11-05] ~~Label the column consistency_with_CDM_terms, not grounded.~~
blocking_status: blocks a grounding-as-validation claim. Corrected finding (2026-11-05). The grounding column is external, so the circularity worry is gone — and with it the project's best defence against the weaker charge that follows. Three unlike measures share one column name, and the manuscript quotes a single number from all of them: 1. ChemicalEntity, DiseaseOrPhenotypicFeature, GeneOrGeneProduct, OrganismTaxon are genuine external-vocabulary lookups over 95 of the 117 cells. These are legitimate Tier-2 precision proxies. 2. SequenceVariant (16 cells) is not a vocabulary lookup at all. ground() returns {"PATTERN"} iff the string matches VARIANT_RE — a surface-format regex for rs…, HGVS-like and substitution-like strings. Its 2.5% pooled rate (1,257 / 50,249 unique strings) measures **how often a model emitted variant-shaped text**, not whether the variant exists. A fabricated rs999999999 scores exactly like a real one. 3. CellLine (19 cells) is definitional 0.0% — ground() returns set() unconditionally. It is a missing vocabulary, not a model result, and appears in the manuscript's figure as a model outcome. Two further denominators the block never stated. (a) Grounding is the share of unique strings, not of mentions: llm_qwen_fs OrganismTaxon is 15.1% of 9,113 distinct strings over **54,139 mentions**, so a model that repeats one grounded surface inflates nothing while a model that emits many near-duplicate wrong surfaces is punished — the metric is a type inventory measure, not a per-occurrence one. (b) corpus_metrics.json ships other_type_pct — the share of a model's strings that ground in a different type than predicted — and neither this report nor the manuscript has ever reported it. It reaches 19.1% (llm_qwen_fs GeneOrGeneProduct) and is above 10% in 9 cells, so for the LLMs a large fraction of "ungrounded" strings are in fact recognisable biomedical names filed under the wrong type. Grounding is therefore type-blind about the error that dominates the LLMs.
